text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 18 in history.
1405 - Pope Pius II born as Aeneas Silvius Piccolomini. He became Pope in 1458 and tried to unite Europe in a crusade against the Turks.
1469 - Isabella of Castile married Ferdinand II of Aragon, thus uniting almost all the Christian dominions of Spain under one monarchy.
1685 - King Louis XIV of France revoked the Edict of Nantes, depriving the Protestant Huguenots of all religious and civil liberties granted them by Henry IV in 1598.
1697 - Canaletto, Italian artist born as Giovanni Antonio Canal. Famous for his views of Venice, London and English country homes.
1748 - The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, negotiated largely by Britain and France, ended the Austrian War of Succession.
1831 - Frederick III (Friedrich Wilhelm Nikolous Karl) born. He reigned as King of Prussia for 99 days in 1888.
1860 - British troops burned the Yuanmingyuan, the imperial summer palace in Beijing, to the ground.
1865 - Lord Palmerston, British statesman and politician, died. He was prime minister twice between 1855 and 1865.
1867 - The U.S. flag flew for the first time at Sitka following the purchase of Alaska from Russia.
1871 - Charles Babbage, British mathematician and inventor who pioneered the forerunner of the computer, died.
1893 - Sir Sidney Holland born. New Zealand statesman who became leader of the National Party in 1940, and prime minister in 1949.
1905 - Felix Houphouet-Boigny, president of the Republic of the Ivory Coast 1960-93, born.
1912 - Italy and Turkey signed a peace treaty at Lausanne, whereby Cyrenaica and Tripoli gained autonomy and the Dodecanese Islands are restored to Turkey.
1919 - Pierre Elliott Trudeau, Canadian statesman, born. Prime Minister 1968-79 and 1980-84.
1922 - In England the British Broadcasting Company (BBC) was formed.
1925 - Melina Mercouri, Greek actress who became a politician and Minister of Culture, born.
1926 - Chuck Berry, U.S. rock and roll pioneer, born.
1931 - Thomas Alva Edison, American inventor, died. In his lifetime he held over 1,000 patents, the most famous being the electric lamp, the phonograph and the motion picture projector.
1939 - Lee Harvey Oswald, assumed assassin of President John F. Kennedy, born.
1956 - Martina Navratilova born. The Czech-born tennis player received political asylum in the U.S.
1963 - Harold Macmillan resigned as British Prime Minister and was replaced by Lord Home who renounced his peerage and became Sir Alec Douglas-Home.
1967 - The Soviet Venera 4 spacecraft entered the atmosphere of Venus and transmitted data back to earth before losing contact 27km above the surface.
1970 - In Canada, the body of Pierre Laporte, the Quebec Minister of Labour, was found following his kidnap by the Quebec Liberation Front.

1977 - Three Palestinian hijackers were killed when a German anti-terrorist squad stormed a Lufthansa aircraft at Mogadishu Airport. All 86 passengers who had been held hostage for five days were freed.
1989 - East Germany leader Erich Honecker stepped down, officially on health grounds, and was replaced by Egon Krenz.
1989 - Hungary's Parliament purged the constitution of its Stalinist elements to create a Western-style basic law for a return to multi-party democracy.
